subject: Measurement framework, reproducibility checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice@acme-analytics.com>; Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Measurement framework, reproducibility checklist & next steps

Hi Alice / Marcus — good to meet you both this morning. Quick recap and proposed continuations from our side so we can align on the benchmark scope before dev work starts.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Acme is validating a streaming chat experience plus batched batch-generation paths for reporting.
- Primary SLO targets you asked for: p95 latency <= 200ms for small (<=128 token) non-streaming replies, streaming chunk latency <= 40ms per chunk, sustained throughput target ~300 req/s for the reporting pipeline (non-streaming), and peak concurrency expected ~60 concurrent sessions.
- Repro concerns: prompt variability, tokenizer differences, and warm vs cold KV cache behavior.

What we propose (actionable):
1) Measurement framework doc: we prepared a lightweight metrics template that separates latency buckets (p50/p95/p99), per-token throughput, and streaming chunk tail metrics. Please review the attached "benchmark-metrics-template.xlsx".
2) Eval harness repo: we will share our reproducibility harness (Docker + test-data) that seeds RNG, pins model checkpoints, and includes a deterministic sampling mode for comparability. Link below and attached a shell stub "eval-harness-repro.sh".
3) Prompt set exchange: please push the initial 50 prompts you want prioritized (we only need text examples and expected acceptance criteria). We attached a sample bundle to illustrate expected JSON shape.
4) Run cadence & responsibilities: Redwood runs an initial baseline suite in our staging region, then we hand off the harness for your infra team to run in your environment. Benchmarks should capture cold-start (first request after restart), warm steady-state, and cache-warmed scenarios.

Questions we still have from our side:
- For streaming: do you define per-chunk size (e.g., 32 tokens) or per-time-slice (e.g., 100ms)?
- Is there a required SLA for first-byte on streaming responses versus steady per-chunk time?

Next steps (proposed):
- Alice: drop first prompt bundle to the shared Drive by EOD Mon Feb 1 (or let us know timeline).
- Redwood: we’ll upload the baseline harness and the metrics spreadsheet to the shared Drive and kick a baseline run against a compatible open model variant.
- Internal: Ben/Aditya to own the first run and produce a short triage doc with any infra/runtime differences noticed.

Attachments: benchmark-metrics-template.xlsx (xlsx, 38 KB); prompt-sample-bundle.json (json, 12 KB); eval-harness-repro.sh (bash, 3 KB)

Thanks — feel free to reply with any immediate corrections; we’ll treat this as the working spec.

—Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Measurement framework, reproducibility checklist & next steps

Naomi — quick internal note to capture what I’ll run and what I’ll hand off.

Plan for the baseline run (this afternoon):
- Model variant: rwght-7b-v2-quant (closest open analog to your expected stack).
- Scenarios: cold-start (container restart then one request), warm-steady (10k requests at target concurrency waveform), streaming-sim (we'll simulate 60 sessions and emit chunks sized to 50 tokens to approximate your UX).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, per-chunk latency distribution, token throughput (tokens/sec), GPU util and mem footprint, and tail time-to-first-byte for streaming.
- Repro flags: seed=42, sample_mode=deterministic, batch_size=1 for latency trials, batch_size up to 8 for throughput trials.

I’ll push results + a short runbook to the Drive under /reports/acme-baseline and will call out any non-deterministic variance > 5% in p95. If we see >10% variance on repeated runs, we’ll capture environment diffs (kernel, driver, cuDNN).

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Alice Thompson <alice@acme-analytics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Measurement framework, reproducibility checklist & next steps

Thanks Naomi — this is exactly the level of detail we wanted. Two clarifications from our product/infra side: 

1) Streaming chunk definition: we prefer per-chunk by token window (we typically render every ~40 tokens in the UI). Please base streaming chunk latency on a 40-token chunk size for SLO purposes.
2) SLA split: we want first-byte streaming <= 120ms (global p95) and subsequent chunk emit <= 50ms median with p95 <= 120ms. For non-streaming small replies we’ll use the p95 <= 200ms target you noted.

We’ll upload the initial 50 prompts by EOD Monday to your Drive link. A couple of constraints from our side to call out:
- For the reporting pipeline the payloads are often 400–600 tokens; we expect throughput validation to include both short (<=128 token) and long (400–600 token) workloads.
- We also want the harness to produce a per-run artifact listing exact model binary checksum and environment (driver versions, container image tag). That’s necessary for our compliance audit.

If all of this looks good we’re happy to have Redwood run the first baseline and then hand the harness to our infra team to reproduce.

Best — Alice
Director of Product | Acme Analytics
alice@acme-analytics.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Measurement framework, reproducibility checklist & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Alice. Action list updated below and I’ll confirm when Ben’s baseline artifacts are uploaded.

Updated actions:
- Acme: upload first-50 prompts to Drive by EOD Mon Feb 1 (Alice).
- Redwood: execute baseline run (Ben) -> upload /reports/acme-baseline including: run-artifacts.tar.gz (model checksum, container tag, driver/kernel), metrics CSV, and raw harness logs.
- Redwood -> Acme: provide a one-click runner (Docker + env file) and the reproducibility checklist so your infra can re-run without changes. Link to repo above.
- Follow-up sync: propose Wed Mar 3, 09:00 PT to review baseline results and decide on any changes to SLO bands or prompt coverage.

I’ll attach Ben’s run report here once it’s in the Drive. If Marcus or your infra team would rather we push the runner as an AMI instead of Docker, let us know and we’ll prepare that artifact.

Thanks — Naomi
